_schema.description: Platform feature positions — which door on a platform is nearest an escalator, lift, stairs, or transfer corridor.
_schema.doorIndex: 1..N counted from the platform's REFERENCE END, which is the end facing the LOWER station code on that line (e.g. the HarbourFront end on the NEL). Direction-independent by design: car numbers are derived at render time by src/lib/doors.ts.
_schema.platformKey: "<stationCode>:<direction>" where direction is "asc" (toward higher station codes) or "desc" (toward lower codes). An island platform has one entry per face.
_schema.source: One of: survey | osm | official-map | user. Required.
_schema.confidence: One of: verified | candidate. Required. Only 'verified' is presented as fact in the UI.
_schema.leadsTo: Exit codes as printed on station signage (e.g. ["C"]), or a line code for a transfer (e.g. "CCL").
_schema.platformSide: Which side of the train the doors open when travelling in this direction, as "left" or "right" FACING THE WAY THE TRAIN IS GOING. Direction-relative rather than screen-relative, so it is unambiguous and matches the on-train announcement. Set explicitly only where the layout cannot imply it.
_schema.orientation: Keyed like platforms: "<stationCode>:<direction>". Requires source and confidence exactly as features do — an unverified guess about which side the doors open is worse than saying nothing.
_schema.platformLayout: One of "island", "side" or "stacked", observed once per station. Singapore runs left-hand, so the layout determines the door side in BOTH directions without surveying each one: an island platform sits to the train's right either way, and side platforms with the tracks between them sit to its left either way. Stacked platforms are one direction per level and can differ, so they carry an explicit side per direction instead.
_schema.layouts: Keyed by station code without direction, since a layout describes the station. Requires source and confidence exactly as everything else does.

_status.note: No platform has been surveyed yet, for door positions or for which side the doors open. No public dataset provides either (verified against LTA DataMall, data.gov.sg, SMRT and SBS Transit), so every entry must come from a field survey or an OSM-derived candidate that a person has then checked. The app shows 'not yet mapped' until an entry exists — it does not estimate.
